_**Agent (default)**_

Great timing for this rewrite. Based on the current code, you **can keep JSON objects for tables/graphs**, but I’d treat the interface as **“stable enough with a hardening pass”**, not fully stable yet.

## Backend-Frontend Contract Stability

What already looks good:
- Many endpoints already return structured JSON, and table endpoints consistently use a `TableData`-style shape (`columns`, `data`, optional `config/metadata`).
- League/team/player/tournament routes are already split by domain, which maps well to a modern SPA.
- Existing docs already define filter combinations and endpoint mapping.

What is currently risky for a full rewrite:
- **Parameter naming inconsistency**: e.g. `team` vs `team_name`, and mixed optional/required patterns.
- **Response envelope inconsistency**: some endpoints return raw arrays/objects, some `TableData`, some `{error: ...}`, some `{message: ...}` with varying status behavior.
- **Chart payload inconsistency**: chart endpoints are not all using one canonical schema.
- Minor signs of legacy drift (debug prints, mixed conventions) suggest accidental contract breaks are possible.

Practical conclusion:
- **Yes, proceed with new frontend**, but first do a small **API contract freeze** so the new UI doesn’t chase moving targets.

## Feature Direction (from your choices)

You selected:
- Scope: **League page first**
- UX priorities: **speed**, **mobile**, **deep-linkable URL state**
- Stack preference: **no strong preference**

That is a very solid v1 scope and lowers migration risk a lot.

## Recommended Tech Stack

For your environment (Win11 local, npm, Unix + systemd + nginx prod), best fit:

- **React + TypeScript + Vite**
- **TanStack Query** for caching/request dedupe/retries (speed)
- **TanStack Router** or `react-router` with typed search params (deep links)
- **Tailwind CSS** (or CSS variables + minimal utility layer) for clean responsive UI
- **ECharts** (or Chart.js if you want parity) for graphs
- **TanStack Table** for interactive tables, while still accepting backend JSON table payloads

Why this stack:
- Fast local dev on Windows, simple static build output for nginx.
- Easy incremental migration (serve SPA from Flask/nginx while keeping old pages alive).
- Strong ecosystem for data-heavy dashboards and extensibility.

## What I’d lock before coding frontend

- Define versioned contracts for league v1 endpoints:
  - `GET /api/v1/league/...`
  - Standard query names: `league`, `season`, `week`, `team`, `database`
- Standardize response shapes:
  - `TableResponse`
  - `ChartResponse`
  - `ListResponse`
  - `ErrorResponse`
- Add a lightweight contract test suite for those endpoints.
- Keep your existing JSON semantics; just normalize and version them.

If you want, next I can draft the **exact v1 API contract** (endpoint list + TS interfaces + error model) for the League page so frontend implementation can start immediately after.

First vertical slice is in and wired.

Implemented:
- New v1 backend blueprint at `app/routes/league_v1_routes.py`
- App registration in `app/__init__.py`
- Route tests in `tests/integration/test_league_v1_routes_flask.py`

### What this slice now exposes

Under `/api/v1/league`:

- `GET /options/leagues` (optional `season`)
- `GET /options/seasons` (requires `league`)
- `GET /options/weeks` (requires `league`, `season`)
- `GET /options/teams` (requires `league`, `season`)
- `GET /season/standings` (requires `league`, `season`)
- `GET /season/team-points` (requires `league`, `season`, optional validated `week`)

### Included in this slice (end-to-end behavior)

- Standard v1 envelope:
  - success: `{ success: true, data, meta }`
  - error: `{ success: false, error, meta }`
- Canonical error codes for validation (`MISSING_REQUIRED_PARAM`, `INVALID_PARAM`)
- Selector caching headers (`ETag`, `Cache-Control`)
- Legacy-to-v1 adapters:
  - table payloads converted to `rows` object format
  - series payloads converted to chart schema (`chartType`, `xAxis`, `yAxis`, `series`, `metadata`)
- Thin adapter approach over existing `LeagueService` (no business logic rewrite)

### Verification status

- Lint diagnostics on edited files: no issues.
- Runtime tests could not be executed here because local tooling is missing:
  - `pytest` not installed in current Python env
  - `python` command alias unavailable, `py` works but lacks `pytest`

### Run locally on your machine

From repo root:

- `py -m pip install pytest`
- `py -m pytest tests/integration/test_league_v1_routes_flask.py`

Quick manual API checks (once app is running):

- `/api/v1/league/options/leagues`
- `/api/v1/league/options/seasons?league=BAYL`
- `/api/v1/league/season/standings?league=BAYL&season=24-25`
- `/api/v1/league/season/team-points?league=BAYL&season=24-25`

If you want, next I’ll add the **frontend-facing smoke page** (tiny static test page hitting only v1 endpoints) so you can visually validate this slice in-browser immediately.

## League v1 Feature Matrix (Charts + Tables)

### Global (applies everywhere)

- **Must Have**
  - Fast loading states (skeleton/spinner + no-layout-jump)
  - Empty/error states with retry action
  - URL-shareable filter state (`league`, `season`, `week`, `team`, `database`)
  - Responsive layout (mobile readable without horizontal chaos)
  - Consistent number formatting (avg/points/percent)

- **Should Have**
  - Light/dark-ready color tokens
  - Keyboard navigation for filters and tables
  - Persisted user prefs (visible columns, sort)

- **Later**
  - Per-user saved dashboard presets
  - Advanced accessibility audits (screen-reader optimized chart summaries)

---

### F1: League Aggregation Block

Endpoints: averages history, points-to-win history, top/record tables

- **Must Have**
  - Line charts with multi-series legend toggle
  - Hover tooltip with exact value + context (season/team)
  - Tables: sort on all numeric columns
  - **Conditional cell coloring** for numeric performance columns
  - **Heatmap mode** optional toggle (color intensity based on value range)

- **Should Have**
  - Zoom/brush for long history
  - “Highlight selected team” overlay across charts
  - Color-scale legend for heatmap interpretation

- **Later**
  - Trendline/regression overlay
  - Percentile bands

---

### F2: Season Overview Block

Endpoints: standings, timetable, individual averages, points/positions/averages charts

- **Must Have**
  - Standings table with sticky header + default sort
  - Points/positions/average line charts with shared x-axis (week)
  - **Row-level conditional formatting** (leader, cutoff zones, relegation bands)
  - **Cell-level coloring** for deltas (up/down, above/below league average)

- **Should Have**
  - Toggle between absolute and relative metrics
  - Mini sparklines in standings rows
  - Season progress indicator (week x of y)

- **Later**
  - Compare 2 teams in split chart mode
  - Animated transitions between weeks

---

### F3: Matchday Block

Endpoints: week standings, honor scores

- **Must Have**
  - Compact week table optimized for quick scanning
  - Honor-score cards with rank emphasis
  - **Conditional badges/colors** for top performances
  - Fast week-switch interaction (no full-page redraw)

- **Should Have**
  - Week-to-week delta indicators
  - “Top N” control for honor cards

- **Later**
  - Matchday story mode (auto-highlight key changes)

---

### F4: Team Week Details Block

Endpoints: classic, individual-scores, head-to-head tables

- **Must Have**
  - View switcher across 3 table modes
  - Stable column grouping and sticky first columns
  - **Per-cell conditional coloring** (won/lost lane, high/low score, clutch cells)
  - **Head-to-head heatmap view** (score or points mode)

- **Should Have**
  - View-mode-specific legend (“what colors mean”)
  - Drilldown row expansion (player details)

- **Later**
  - Side-by-side compare two weeks

---

## Heatmap & Conditional Coloring Spec (proposed baseline)

- **Must Have (v1)**
  - 3 scale types:
    - sequential (low->high)
    - diverging (below/above reference)
    - categorical (win/loss/tie)
  - Normalization scope toggle:
    - table-global
    - column-local
  - Always show legend + min/max/reference marker
  - Color + text contrast guard (auto text color)
  - Disable coloring toggle for accessibility/readability

- **Should Have**
  - User-selectable palette presets
  - Percentile-based normalization option

- **Later**
  - Custom rule builder per column

---

## Recommended v1 implementation cut (practical)

- **Phase A (now)**
  - Tables: sort/filter + conditional cell coloring engine
  - Charts: line charts with legend/tooltip
  - One heatmap (team-vs-team or head-to-head)

- **Phase B**
  - Shared chart interactions + color legends
  - Row-level status coloring in standings

- **Phase C**
  - Advanced normalization/palette controls

## Backlog (P0/P1/P2) with acceptance criteria

## P0 — MVP usable for real analysis

### P0.1 Filter + URL State Core
- **Scope**
  - Stable filter bar for `database`, `league`, `season`, `week`, `team`
  - URL sync + restore on reload/share
- **Endpoints**
  - `/options/leagues`, `/options/seasons`, `/options/weeks`, `/options/teams`
- **Done when**
  - Changing filters updates URL
  - Opening shared URL restores full filter state
  - Selector dependencies refresh correctly (league -> seasons, season -> weeks/teams)

---

### P0.2 Season Standings Table Foundation
- **Scope**
  - Render `/season/standings`
  - Column sort, sticky header, loading/empty/error states
- **Done when**
  - Default sort applies consistently
  - Top 10+ rows render without layout break
  - Empty response shows friendly placeholder, not crash

---

### P0.3 Team Points Line Chart Foundation
- **Scope**
  - Render `/season/team-points` as line chart
  - Legend toggle + tooltip baseline
- **Done when**
  - Multiple series render correctly
  - User can hide/show a team series
  - Tooltip shows week + value + team

---

### P0.4 Conditional Cell Coloring Engine (Table Core)
- **Scope**
  - Generic cell-color rule layer for numeric table columns
  - Sequential and diverging modes
- **Done when**
  - At least 2 table columns use conditional color
  - Contrast guard keeps text readable
  - Coloring can be toggled off

---

### P0.5 **Team-vs-Team Heatmap (your priority)**
- **Scope**
  - Add team-vs-team matrix view as the flagship heatmap
  - Toggle metric (score/points where available)
  - Legend + normalization mode
- **Endpoint**
  - Use v1 season compare endpoint (add if missing in shell wiring)
- **Done when**
  - Matrix renders all teams in selected league/season
  - Color legend visible with min/max
  - Hover shows row team, col team, metric value
  - Diagonal cells handled explicitly (blank or neutral)
  - Works on desktop and is usable on mobile (scroll container)

---

### P0.6 Matchday Snapshot
- **Scope**
  - Render `/matchday/standings` + `/matchday/honor-scores`
- **Done when**
  - Week switch updates both blocks together
  - Error in one block does not break the other

---

### P0.7 Team Week Trio
- **Scope**
  - Wire `/team-week/classic`, `/individual-scores`, `/head-to-head`
  - Segmented view switcher
- **Done when**
  - Switching views is instant and keeps filters
  - Each table has consistent column behavior and empty/error handling

---

## P1 — Quality + analysis power

### P1.1 Advanced Table UX
- Column visibility, resize, pin first column
- Export CSV current view
- **Done when** user can personalize table and export exactly visible data

### P1.2 Advanced Chart UX
- Zoom/brush + reset
- Shared crosshair between season charts
- **Done when** user can inspect dense seasons without losing context

### P1.3 Heatmap Enhancements
- Normalization toggle (`global` vs `column`)
- Palette presets
- **Done when** same matrix can be interpreted in at least 2 valid analytical modes

### P1.4 Performance Hardening
- Request dedupe + cache windows
- Virtualized rows for large tables
- **Done when** interactions stay smooth on realistic max datasets

---

## P2 — polish / advanced features

### P2.1 Personalization
- Saved views/presets
- “favorite teams” quick pins

### P2.2 Comparative analytics
- Overlay two seasons
- Delta heatmap (this season vs last)

### P2.3 Accessibility deep pass
- Keyboard-complete table interactions
- Non-visual chart summary narration

In `frontend-shell/src/index.css`:
- Added styling for grouped heatmap blocks and titles.

For team-vs-team heatmap:
- No more flattened contrast due to mixed metric ranges.
- Points and score-like metrics get meaningful color intensity independently.
- You can still switch back to single-map mode if needed.

_**Agent (default)**_

Fixed — honor cards are now robust and should no longer crash the frontend.

### What was wrong
The UI assumed `honor-scores` always returned an array in `data.cards`, but backend payloads can be object-shaped (grouped keys) or mixed. That mismatch caused render errors.

### What I changed

In `frontend-shell/src/App.tsx`:

- Replaced strict array handling with a safe normalizer:
  - `normalizeHonorCards(raw)`
  - supports:
    - array payloads
    - object payloads (keyed groups)
    - mixed nested objects/arrays/primitives
- Added fallback behavior:
  - if a card can’t be mapped cleanly, it renders raw JSON for that card instead of crashing
- Added cleaner card rendering:
  - title + bullet items (`label: value`)

In `frontend-shell/src/index.css`:
- Added styling for new honor-card title and list format.

### Result
- Honor scores now render safely across variable payload shapes.
- Unknown structures degrade gracefully instead of throwing runtime errors.

If it still errors on your current data, paste one sample `honor-scores` payload and I’ll tighten the formatter exactly to that schema.
